mission_08: Keyword spotting (KWS) is the task of detecting specific trigger words or phrases in continuous audio streams, enabling voice-activated systems like wake word detection for smart speakers. Unlike full speech recognition, KWS focuses on detecting a small set of predefined keywords with very low latency and minimal computational resources, making it suitable for always-on edge devices. The standard approach uses MFCC features as input to a compact neural network, typically a Depthwise Separable Convolutional Neural Network (DS-CNN) that achieves high accuracy with low parameter count. Depthwise separable convolutions factor a standard convolution into a depthwise convolution (applying a single filter per input channel) followed by a pointwise convolution (1x1 convolution across channels), dramatically reducing computation. The sliding window approach processes overlapping audio segments, extracting features and classifying each window, then aggregating detections across time. A confidence threshold filters out low-confidence predictions, and temporal smoothing can reduce false triggers. In this mission, you will implement MFCC feature extraction, DS-CNN layers with batch normalization and ReLU, a complete keyword spotting model, and a sliding window detection system.
